python3 -c "
import parse

# Parse +0100 (no colon)
r = parse.parse('{:ti}', 'a 1997-07-16T19:20+0100 b')
print('Parsed +0100:')
print('  datetime:', r.fixed[0])
print('  tzinfo:', r.fixed[0].tzinfo)
print('  tzname:', r.fixed[0].tzinfo.tzname(None))

# Create expected with +01:00 format
expected = parse.FixedTzOffset(60, '+01:00')
print()
print('Expected FixedTzOffset(60, \"+01:00\"):')
print('  name:', expected.tzname(None))
print('  offset:', expected.utcoffset(None))

# Compare
print()
print('Are they equal?', r.fixed[0].tzinfo == expected)
"

```python
def __eq__(self, other):
    return self._name == other._name and self._offset == other._offset
```

So two FixedTzOffset instances are equal only if both their names AND offsets match. This means if I parse "+01:00" and compare it to a FixedTzOffset(60, '+0100'), they won't be equal even though the offset is the same!
